title: Spectrogram Waterfall Display
description: A scrolling colour-mapped frequency-versus-time display with four example sound sequences showing their characteristic signatures.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Time-Frequency Analysis
Spectrum Display

learningObjectives: Interpret a changing pitch as a moving trace
Explain why a transient appears as a vertical stripe
prerequisites: A spectrum is magnitude per bin

assumptions: 48 bins spanning 0 to 8 kHz, 180 precomputed frames per example
Deterministic broadband texture for the clap so captures are reproducible
limitations: Spectra are synthesized rather than computed from audio; the shapes are representative rather than measured

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Recognizable sounds paired with their visual signatures
keyQuestions: Why is a clap a vertical stripe rather than a horizontal line?
What sets the thickness of the whistle's trace?
commonMisconceptions: That a transient has one frequency
That trace thickness indicates loudness rather than resolution
assessmentOpportunities: Identify a sound from a described set of horizontal traces
